name: NY-22
label: Safe D

key_factors: Markets price Mannion at 93-94% to win
Mannion has a 10-to-1 fundraising advantage and large cash lead
District leans Democratic by 4 points with a favorable national environment for Democrats
No public polling of the general election
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Mannion: a D+4 district, incumbency, a Democratic-tilted environment, and a dominant fundraising edge over Buller, who has raised only about $267,000. Prediction markets on Kalshi and Polymarket both price the Democrat near 94%, consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Mannion or a strong Republican wave would be the main threats to this rating.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
John Mannion, the Democratic incumbent, seeks a second term in a Syracuse-area district that leans Democratic by about four points. He enters the general election with a decisive financial advantage, having raised roughly $2.7 million and holding $1.8 million on hand, while Republican Kailee Buller has raised about $267,000 with limited cash remaining. No outside groups have spent meaningfully in the race so far.

There is no public general-election polling, so the outlook rests on fundamentals and market pricing. Kalshi and Polymarket both put Mannion's chances in the low-to-mid 90s. With the incumbent's resources, the district lean, and a favorable environment, the race is rated Safe Democratic, though uncertainty is somewhat elevated given the absence of polling.
